---
title: "Part 3 - HLAtools"
---

# HLAtools is an R package for working with the IPD-IMGT/HLA Database: allele names, versions, and the sequence alignments. We'll use it to look at HLA-DPB1 protein sequences, which sets us up for the app at the end.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(HLAtools)
```

# Download the DPB1 protein alignment straight from the IPD-IMGT/HLA Database (this needs an internet connection and takes a few seconds). Asking for a specific database version means we get the same answer every time. The other HLAtools functions look for an object named "HLAalignments", so that's what we call it.

```{r}
HLAalignments <- alignmentFull(loci = "DPB1", alignType = "prot", version = "3.65.0")
```

# Compare a few alleles side by side at the positions that make up two of the major DPB1 antibody epitopes (55 to 57 and 84 to 87).

```{r}
customAlign(
  "prot",
  c("DPB1*02:01:02:01", "DPB1*03:01:01:01", "DPB1*04:01:01:01", "DPB1*04:02:01:01"),
  c(55:57, 84:87)
)
```

# That used to mean downloading a text file and counting columns by hand. HLAtools has more where that came from: compareSequences() lists every position where two alleles differ, queryPositions() counts the residues at a position across all alleles, and motifMatch() finds every allele carrying a motif. See ?HLAtools.
